**UKPI launches commercial variable recurring payments scheme**

*GoCardless is the first provider live on the new UK Payments Initiative scheme for recurring account-to-account payments, giving the domestic alternative to cards its first concrete product rails.*

The UK Payments Initiative has gone live with a shared rulebook, commercial model and operating standards for variable recurring payments. GoCardless is the scheme's first active participant, offering what it calls "Recurring Pay by Bank", which pairs real-time API-initiated payments with mandate management for subscriptions and regular billing.

This matters because UKPI has been discussed primarily as an ambition since the UK's largest banks backed the scheme in late May. The launch of a functioning commercial framework, rather than just a governance structure, is the step that turns it into something merchants and payment service providers can actually build on. Variable recurring payments have long been seen as the use case most likely to drive open banking payment volumes beyond one-off transactions, but have lacked a common scheme to make them interoperable across banks and intermediaries.

The scheme's success will depend on bank adoption beyond the initial participants and on whether the commercial model offers merchants a compelling enough saving over card-on-file billing. GoCardless's early participation is notable given its existing direct debit business, positioning it to migrate existing mandates onto faster, data-richer rails.

*Sources: [GoCardless Launches Recurring Pay by Bank as part of New UK Payment Scheme](https://ffnews.com/newsarticle/paytech/gocardless-launches-recurring-pay-by-bank-as-part-of-new-uk-payment-scheme/) — Fintech Finance News | [UKPI launches new open banking payment framework](https://www.fintechfutures.com/open-banking/uk-banks-and-fintechs-unite-to-launch-new-open-banking-payment-framework) — FinTech Futures | [GoCardless backs UKPI scheme launch to drive recurring open banking payments](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/gocardless-backs-ukpi-scheme-launch-to-drive-recurring-open-banking-payments) — The Paypers | [UK Payments Initiative launches recurring bank scheme](https://itbrief.co.uk/story/uk-payments-initiative-launches-recurring-bank-scheme) — IT Brief UK*

stories.original:
**Mastercard adds stablecoin settlement to its merchant network**

*Mastercard will allow merchants and acquirers to settle transactions in stablecoins, extending digital asset rails from niche crypto use cases into mainstream payment flows.*

Mastercard announced at Money20/20 Europe that it is expanding its settlement capabilities to include stablecoin-denominated settlement for merchants. The move lets acquirers and merchants receive funds in stablecoins rather than traditional fiat currencies, integrating digital asset settlement into Mastercard's existing network infrastructure.

The significance is less about crypto adoption and more about settlement optionality. Stablecoin settlement can reduce the number of intermediaries in cross-border merchant payouts, potentially compressing costs and settlement times. For Mastercard, it also represents a defensive play: as account-to-account and blockchain-based payment alternatives gain traction, embedding stablecoin settlement into the card network keeps volume within Mastercard's ecosystem rather than ceding it to standalone crypto payment providers.

This follows Mastercard's recent participation in the ECB's cross-currency instant payments pilot, signalling a broader strategy of positioning the network as infrastructure-agnostic, capable of routing value across card rails, instant payment systems and now digital asset networks.

*Sources: [Mastercard expands settlement capabilities](https://www.mastercard.com/us/en/news-and-trends/press/2026/june/mastercard-expands-settlement-capabilities-to-include-stablecoin.html) — Mastercard*

**ING brings Wero online payments to 10 million German customers**

*ING's expansion of Wero to e-commerce in Germany marks the scheme's most significant retail distribution milestone, testing whether EPI's account-to-account alternative can gain traction at online checkout.*

ING will extend support for Wero, the European Payments Initiative's account-to-account payment method, to online shopping for its 10 million German customers. Until now, Wero's rollout has focused on peer-to-peer transfers. Moving into e-commerce is the use case that will determine whether EPI can genuinely challenge card networks at the point of sale.

Germany is a strategic market for this expansion. German consumers already show a strong preference for non-card payment methods such as PayPal, Klarna and direct bank transfers via Giropay (which Wero is replacing). ING's large German customer base gives Wero immediate scale, but the real test is merchant acceptance: online retailers need a reason to integrate another payment method, which means Wero must offer either lower costs, higher conversion rates or both.

The move follows a pattern of EPI participants activating Wero in their home markets after the peer-to-peer launch phase. France and Belgium have seen similar progressions. Germany's size and existing appetite for alternative payments make it the most consequential test yet.

*Sources: [ING expands Wero payments to online shopping in Germany](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47852/ing-expands-wero-payments-to-online-shopping-in-germany) — Finextra*

**ECB's Cipollone calls for active push to strengthen euro's global payments role**

*ECB executive board member Piero Cipollone has urged Europe to accelerate digital payment infrastructure and capital markets integration to bolster the euro's international standing, framing payments autonomy as essential to monetary sovereignty.*

Piero Cipollone used a speech to argue that Europe must move beyond passive reliance on external payment infrastructure and actively strengthen the euro's role in global transactions. He pointed to the rapid growth of instant payments following EU legislation and the Eurosystem's pan-European TIPS infrastructure as evidence that coordinated action works, but warned that rising competition from other currencies and payment systems demands further urgency.

The speech builds on a theme Cipollone and other ECB officials have pressed consistently this year: that European payment sovereignty is not an abstract policy goal but a practical requirement for monetary independence. His framing positions instant payments, digital euro work and schemes such as Wero as components of a single strategic effort rather than separate initiatives.

For the industry, the message is that ECB pressure on banks and payment providers to adopt European infrastructure will intensify. Cipollone's remarks also signal that the ECB sees the competitive landscape, including stablecoin-based settlement and non-European instant payment networks, as a direct challenge to euro-denominated payment flows.

*Sources: [ECB Board Member calls on Europe to actively strengthen the euro's global role](https://www.cbn.com.cy/article/129919/ecb-board-member-calls-on-europe-to-actively-strengthen-the-euro-s-global-role) — CBN*

**UK Government Digital Service picks Adyen for open banking on Gov.UK Pay**

*The UK's Government Digital Service has appointed Adyen to add open banking payments to the Gov.UK Pay platform, bringing account-to-account payments into public sector transactions.*

GDS has selected Adyen to deliver open banking payment functionality on Gov.UK Pay, the centralised payment platform used by government departments and local authorities. The integration will allow citizens to pay for public services directly from their bank accounts, bypassing card networks.

This is a notable reference case for pay-by-bank in the UK. Government payments are high-volume, low-margin transactions where the cost savings from avoiding card interchange are material. If the integration works well, it creates a visible, trusted example of account-to-account payments in everyday use, potentially accelerating consumer familiarity with the payment method.

Adyen's appointment is also significant competitively. The company has been building out its open banking capabilities alongside its core card acquiring business, and a government contract provides both scale and credibility. The move aligns with the FCA's broader open finance agenda, which has emphasised expanding data sharing and payment initiation beyond retail financial services.

*Sources: [GDS appoints Adyen to bring open banking to Gov.UK Pay](https://www.globalgovernmentfinance.com/gds-govukpay-adyen-open-banking/) — Global Government Finance*
